title: On Blaming the youngest boy first
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：blame　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 blame 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1969 the driver ① blamed the youngest boy first on the same day, and every passenger in the station said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three days on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the driver ② blames the youngest boy first before dawn without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ blame the youngest boy first at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ blamed the youngest boy first before — a line in the timetable for February 1963 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Blaming the youngest boy first on the same day, the driver said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the ticket at the far platform, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ blame the delay on the rain before dawn, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Blame the delay on the rain at once and never mention it again.

By 1976 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the timetable, and a new passenger from the next station ⑧ blames the delay on the rain on the same day every day without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the platform, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ blamed the youngest boy first again when nobody else would.

⑩ To blame the youngest boy first, my mother said in 1981, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the station remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the station forgets, somebody blames the youngest boy first before dawn again and somebody must blame the youngest boy first on the same day all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 责备（一般过去式 blamed the youngest boy first：1969 年司机头一回这样做，当天就）
B. v. 责备（一般现在 blames the youngest boy first：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 责备（不定式 to blame the youngest boy first：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 责备（过去完成时 had blamed the youngest boy first：1963 年二月的时刻表上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 责备（动名词 blaming the youngest boy first 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 归咎（blame the delay on the rain：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去归咎把延误归到那场雨上）
G. v. 归咎（blame the delay on the rain：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 责备（后段两处：新来的乘客照例 blames the delay on the rain，而母亲又一次 blamed the youngest boy first）

answers.why: blame 意为“责备”，1969 年司机当天就责备头一个责备最小的男孩，那是车站里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 blamed。
blame 意为“责备”，自那以后司机天没亮就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 blames。
blame 意为“责备”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯责备头一个责备最小的男孩”，此处为不定式 to blame the youngest boy first。
blame 意为“责备”，时刻表里 二月 那行字说明早在 1976 年之前就有人责备过，故用过去完成时 had blamed。
blame 意为“责备”，司机说“责备头一个责备最小的男孩这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 blaming the youngest boy first 作主语。
blame 意为“归咎”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去归咎把延误归到那场雨上”，should ever 之后用原形 blame the delay on the rain。
blame 意为“归咎”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻归咎把延误归到那场雨上（blame the delay on the rain at once），以后再也不要提起。
blame 意为“责备”，新来的乘客每个日子都照例归咎把延误归到那场雨上，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 blames。
blame 意为“责备”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当天就责备头一个责备最小的男孩，用一般过去式 blamed 叙述。
blame 意为“责备”，结尾那句是母亲 1981 年的话：要责备头一个责备最小的男孩，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和车站记住的那一件。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1969 年，司机当天就责备头一个责备最小的男孩；车站里每一个乘客都说这是头一回。（blamed the youngest boy first）
多年以后，司机仍天没亮就做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（blames the youngest boy first）
母亲后来说，难就难在肯责备头一个责备最小的男孩这件事本身。（to blame the youngest boy first）
早在 1963 年就有人责备头一个责备最小的男孩，二月那天时刻表上的一行字就是证据。（had blamed the youngest boy first）
司机说过，当天就责备头一个责备最小的男孩这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（blaming the youngest boy first 作主语）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 blame 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1969 the driver blamed the youngest boy first on the same day, and nobody in the station forgot it.
Even now the driver blames the youngest boy first before dawn whenever the station asks.
Blaming the youngest boy first on the same day, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever blame the delay on the rain before dawn, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new passenger from the next station blames the delay on the rain on the same day every day, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother blamed the youngest boy first again, and the station remembered that half.
